body.statement: For every \(C=(G,\Pi),D=(H,\Lambda)\in\mathfrak S_p\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\); \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\), equivalently \(G,H\) have the same skeleton and unshielded colliders, \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for all \(j\in V\), and every edge joining vertices with unequal nonsingleton families has the same orientation; and \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\). Every step in the final characterization is a partition-compatible singleton covered reversal with the prescribed transport. Moreover, \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D)\), and a shortest path reverses each disagreeing arrow exactly once. When every block is nonsingleton, \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\), recovering and strictly extending the BPEC structural-identifiability result of BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 to the singleton-allowing blocked class.
body.justification: The theorem supplies both an exact static recovery functional and a complete local transformation calculus for the largest target-blocked coefficient class that contains ordinary DAG equivalence.
body.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Theorem 5.17, excludes singleton edge-colour classes and Question 5.19 asks for graphical edge-coloured equivalence; Chickering1995, Theorem 2, transports ordinary DAGs but has no coefficient-partition legality condition.
body.consumer: An extension of the colouredDAGs workflow can report the exact covariance-equivalence component instead of one arbitrary blocked DAG while retaining all repeated-coefficient communities.
